parts.title: Part 4
parts.annotated_transcript_html:
As a result, many Berbers left their settlements to lead a nomadic life by wandering with their animals through the deserts and across the different mountains. [Q31]

They are called seasonal nomads. [Q32]

A third group settled by the oases and grew fruit and vegetables like dates and eggplants as well as making olive oil which they used for cooking. [Q33]

So the Berbers relied more and more on camels for transporting their families and their goods. [Q34]

As you might expect though, the life of a settled community was governed by the men who met regularly in the village square to discuss affairs and make decisions. [Q35]

If the skins weren't available, they wove mats made of grass or palm leaves and hung them over a frame so that the tent looked like a humped dome. [Q36]

Tuareg society was traditionally very feudal and organised as a strict hierarchy ranging from nobles or aristocrats downwards to labourers whose ancestors had once been slaves. [Q37]

Tuareg men were sometimes called blue men as all adult males wore a dark blue veil in the presence of women, strangers and in-laws. [Q38]

Those whose animals were fortunate enough to survive have moved away from the southern Sahara into Burkina Faso in order to find new grazing lands for their herds. [Q39]

The tourism department of the Mali government employs some Tuaregs who act as guides. [Q40]
